function.arguments: {"contract_model": "[\"Compute a single normalized RBF regression prediction for one fixed float32 workload from make_inputs(): query (32,), anchors (16,32), values (16,).\", \"Reference is defined in float64 from stored float32 values: distance = sum_k (a[i,k]-q[k])^2, weight = exp(-16*distance), output = sum(w*v)/sum(w).\", \"Error metric: ||output-ref||_2 / max(||ref||_2, 0.05) must be <= 0.05; only final normalized prediction matters, not intermediates.\", \"Only alternative-input/seed behaviors are out of scope.\"], \"kernel_model</arg_key><arg_value>[\"Triton kernel launched with a single program, N=16, D=32, num_warps=1, enable_fp_fusion=False; writes one float32 output.\", \"Computes expanded squared distance ||a||^2 + ||q||^2 - 2 a.q per anchor, accumulating in float32 (anchor_norm, query_norm, dot) via tl.static_range over D=32.\", \"Clamps computed distance at 0 (tl.maximum) before exp(-16*distance); weights sum to numerator/denominator in float32 with div_rn.\", \"Inputs are near the query (anchors = query + N(0, 0.015625)), query entries ~16, so true distances are tiny (~D*sigma^2 ~ 0.008) but anchor norms ~ 16^2*32 ~ 8192, making the expanded form heavily catastrophic-cancellation prone in float32.\", \"Make_inputs uses a fixed PCG64 seed 119263 and float64 perturbation then cast to float32; same for query and values.\"], \"risk_map</arg_key><arg_value>[\"Catastrophic cancellation in float32 expanded-distance: norm_sum and twice_dot are ~8192-scale while their difference is ~1e-3; fp32 ulp error (~0.001 at 8192) is comparable to or larger than the true distance, so computed distances can be wildly wrong or clamped to 0.\", \"Even though clamping prevents negative distances, wrong (large or zero) distances feed exp(-16*d); if all distances clamp to 0, weights all become 1 and output equals mean(values), which may or may not be within 5% relative tolerance of the true weighted prediction.\", \"Sequential float32 accumulation of dot products over 32 terms adds rounding, but the dominant risk is cancellation, not accumulation.\", \"div_rn and exp in fp32 add small additional error; likely subdominant.\"], \"scope_notes</arg_key><arg_value>[\"Single fixed workload (seed 119263) only; robustness to other inputs/seeds is out of scope.\", \"Contract tolerates up to 5% relative error (denominator floored at 0.05) on the final scalar, so large per-weight errors can still pass if the normalized prediction is close.\", \"Normalization may mask biased distances: if all weights are equal (all d clamped to 0), output = mean(values); reference with true small distances is also near a weighted mean with nearly equal weights, so cancellation may be hidden by normalization.\"], \"summary</arg_key><arg_value>Describe case_z: single-point normalized RBF regression kernel using expanded squared-distance in fp32 with clamping; key risk is catastrophic cancellation between large anchor/query norms and dot product."}
